narration: A delayed truck puts the next pickup at risk. RoadStar lets a dispatcher rehearse the recovery, approve a feasible replacement, and keep the driver and detention evidence connected. This is the working synthetic rehearsal.
screen: Original studio road sculpture and shared RoadStar title

narration: A carrier is coordinating loads, drivers, trucks, trailers, appointment windows, and duty time. A dock delay changes several of those commitments at once. RoadStar brings that decision into one workspace. The dispatcher can see the affected assignment and compare a replacement before changing the plan. Every demonstration shipment is explicitly synthetic.
screen: Animated explanatory route and dock-delay branch

narration: Here, Alex is delayed on the first trip. Recording the expected departure exposes the next assignment at risk. The original commitment stays visible while we prepare a recovery. We select Morgan with a different truck and trailer. RoadStar checks availability, equipment, declared duty budgets, and truck-route travel time. The route comes from Valhalla using Ontario road data and the supplied vehicle dimensions. Missing evidence or an infeasible choice stays visible.
screen: Verified 3D dock/corridor evidence and server-ranked replacement result

narration: The recovery review shows the existing assignment, the proposed replacement, and the evidence used to make the comparison. The dispatcher approves this revision. At that moment, the server checks the current versions and availability again. If the driver or resource evidence changed, approval returns a conflict. A successful approval updates assignments, reservations, and the driver offer in one database transaction. Repeated commands retain their original idempotency key.
screen: Verified recovery outcome, rejected HOS candidate and consequential approval review

narration: The driver receives a manifest with the next action, stop instructions, and trip context. Acceptance is recorded separately from dispatch. On the Android emulator, we also tested losing connectivity: acceptance stayed visibly pending, survived a force-stop, and synchronized after reconnecting without another assignment. The native app preserves downloaded work and encrypted sign-in state. Tracking is an explicit work-session choice. Physical phone background-location testing and native iOS verification are still deferred.
screen: Standalone Android emulator Today, actual Valhalla map and persistent queue

narration: The same shipment keeps its document and detention context. This source PDF is stored privately, hashed, and extracted with Gemini. A dispatcher reviews corrections without replacing the original extraction. Reviewed arrival instructions retain their source. Detention uses arrival and departure samples for the same stop and configured contract terms. The reviewer must acknowledge the observed-sample precision. Approval creates a new invoice revision and preserves the draft. It does not collect a payment or turn uncertain GPS into an exact timestamp.
screen: Actual reviewed document, facility lineage and retained detention invoice evidence

narration: RoadStar also plans shared routes. These two less-than-truckload shipments fit one selected vehicle. OR-Tools uses actual truck-route matrices to order both pickups and deliveries while checking the supported capacity and time constraints. The dispatcher reviews the assumptions before approving. The driver accepts one complete manifest, and the app enforces its global stop order. Vehicle reservations remain active until all deliveries are complete. This preview discloses its synthetic pallet-capacity allowance.
screen: Actual approved OR-Tools plan, route-matrix evidence and assumptions

narration: The importer reconciled all five supplied workbook sheets: over fifteen thousand source rows, including eighty-two exact duplicate dispatch rows. Original rows, missing fields, historical dates, and normalized records retain their lineage. Customer data remains isolated locally. The public preview uses synthetic scenarios for missing operational inputs. Scenario replay has its own clock and identical starting conditions, so modeled comparisons cannot overwrite live operational time.
screen: Source reconciliation counts with synthetic/public data boundary

narration: The deployed platform uses Firebase identity, Cloud Run services, PostgreSQL with PostGIS, private Cloud Storage, Cloud Tasks, and Vertex AI. Database tests cover overlapping reservations, stale approvals, repeated commands, role boundaries, and uncertain telemetry. A cloud burst representing one hundred thirty-one drivers completed without failed commands, but measured about five point four seconds of synchronization lag at the ninety-fifth percentile. That is a measured limit, not a two-second service guarantee.
screen: Measured verification and disclosed synchronization limitation

narration: RoadStar connects recovery decisions to execution and evidence. The next step is physical-device validation and carrier evaluation of the complete workflow. Open the preview to rehearse a recovery, inspect the assumptions, and follow the approved change through to the driver.
screen: Studio route sculpture and preview invitation
